documents.title: Large Cap Fund - Scheme Information
documents.content: The Large Cap Fund is an open-ended equity scheme predominantly investing in large cap stocks. Investment objective: achieve long-term capital appreciation by investing in a diversified portfolio of equity and equity-related instruments of large cap companies. Benchmark: a broad large cap index TRI. Minimum SIP amount: Rs 500. Exit load: 1% if redeemed within 12 months. Risk level: Very High. Suitable for investors with an investment horizon of 5+ years.

documents.title: Small Cap Fund - Scheme Information Document
documents.content: The Small Cap Fund is an open-ended equity scheme predominantly investing in small cap stocks. Investment objective: long-term capital appreciation from a portfolio of small cap companies. Benchmark: a small cap index TRI. Minimum SIP amount: Rs 100. Exit load: 1% if redeemed within 12 months (10% of units exempt). Risk level: Very High. Higher volatility; suitable for investors with high risk tolerance and 5+ year horizon.

documents.title: Liquid Fund - Scheme Information
documents.content: The Liquid Fund is an open-ended liquid scheme investing in money market and debt instruments with maturity up to 91 days. Objective: provide a high level of liquidity with reasonable returns. Benchmark: a liquid index. Risk level: Low to Moderate. Ideal for parking surplus funds for short durations. Relatively low interest rate risk and moderate credit risk.

documents.title: ELSS Tax Saver Fund - Scheme Information
documents.content: The ELSS Tax Saver Fund is an open-ended equity linked savings scheme with a statutory lock-in of 3 years and tax benefit under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act. Objective: generate long-term capital appreciation. Benchmark: a broad market index TRI. Minimum SIP amount: Rs 500. Risk level: Very High. Investments up to Rs 1.5 lakh per year qualify for 80C deduction.

documents.title: KYC process for mutual fund investments
documents.content: KYC (Know Your Customer) is mandatory for mutual fund investments in India. You can complete KYC online (e-KYC) using your PAN and Aadhaar via a KRA (KYC Registration Agency). Documents required: PAN card, Aadhaar, a recent photograph, and address proof. KYC status can be checked on any KRA website using your PAN. Once KYC is verified, it is valid across all SEBI-registered mutual funds.

documents.title: What is a SIP and how to start one
documents.content: A Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) lets you invest a fixed amount at regular intervals (e.g. monthly). Benefits: rupee cost averaging and the power of compounding. To start a SIP: complete KYC, choose a scheme, select the SIP amount (minimum Rs 500) and date, and set up an auto-debit mandate (e-mandate/NACH). You can pause, modify, or stop a SIP anytime.

documents.title: How to redeem mutual fund units
documents.content: To redeem units, log in to the fund house portal or app, select the scheme, and enter the amount or number of units to redeem. Redemption proceeds are credited to your registered bank account. Equity funds: T+2 settlement. Liquid/debt funds: T+1. Note any applicable exit load and capital gains tax. ELSS units can only be redeemed after the 3-year lock-in.
